title: The hewers gather at Àth leathan
body: Hewers of the five western towns gather at Àth leathan, where the road from the south enters the hills. The Board's lists name Ruth Calder and Tom Varley among them.

title: The regiments go west
body: The regiments set out from Cathair dhearg by the western road, their carts and lorries running on dubhan, to join the enforcers at Seann Skell in the west.

title: Battle of Àth leathan
body: The first great battle of An Cogadh Fada, the Long War. The state, whose failing power already leans on Dubhan's fuel, moves against the holdouts in arms.

title: The dead of Àth leathan
body: The open record counts the kingdom's dead at Àth leathan and not the holdouts'. The Tuathaich tellings put theirs in the hundreds. After this battle Ruth Calder's name is not found in the open record.

title: Into the hills
body: After Àth leathan the holdouts give up the southern pits and fall back into the hills about Muileann àrsaidh and Cnoc thais. The pits at Àth leathan are taken without a fight and flooded by the Board's order.

title: An seachdamh rèisimeid raised
body: The seventh regiment is raised from the levies of the west coast and stationed at Seann Skell, the river port nearest the western hills. It holds the road behind the army and the field of Àth leathan.

title: The field of Àth leathan after
body: The field of Àth leathan is left unploughed. The patrols of the seventh regiment pass it on the road to the western hills and report it empty.

title: The wartime tithe
body: For the war a tax is laid, for a time, on every sale of dubhan in the kingdom. It is never lifted after the war ends.

title: The tithe at the pumps
body: The wartime tithe is taken at the dubhan depots, where a clerk of the Treasury sits beside every pump. Within a month the fair-court at Muileann òg records the first complaint against it.

title: A' chiad rèisimeid raised
body: The first regiment is raised at Inis mhòr, the river port beside the capital, from the capital's own companies. It guards the council, the mint and the bridge over the Abhainn dhomhain.

title: A' chiad chabhlach raised
body: The first fleet is raised from the south-west harbours and stationed at Àth gharbh, its hulls lying in the harbour of Doire shean a short walk away. It is sent round the western cape to stop the coal going out by sea from the Tuathaich ports.

title: An ceathramh cabhlach raised
body: The fourth fleet is raised at Cuan shean on the west coast and joins the first off the Tuathaich shore. Between them they close Seann Skell and Cnoc bhàn in the north-west to every boat but fishing boats, and search those.

title: The siege of Muileann àrsaidh
body: The regiments lay siege to Muileann àrsaidh. The town holds for weeks on stored coal and potatoes, and its pit-heads are taken one by one. Sìleas nic Rath's open record gives the day it fell and nothing else.

title: An treas rèisimeid raised
body: The third regiment is raised at Cathair mhòr, where the Mine Board keeps its offices in the old stone house of Mac Ùisdein. Its first muster is held under the market cross the house raised.

title: An còigeamh rèisimeid raised
body: The fifth regiment is raised at Seann Warr on the lake shore west of the capital. It is sent north to relieve the regiments before Muileann àrsaidh.

title: The capital's lamp-houses rationed
body: Dubhan for the army is taken before every other use. The poorer streets of the capital go dark again, as they were before the fuel came, and the lamp-houses of Cathair dhearg ration it street by street.

title: Families at Caol mhòr
body: Families from the western pits come into Caol mhòr and Doire ghlas with what they can carry. The Moot feeds them from its own stores, as it resolved to do. The council sends nothing and forbids nothing.

title: The Moot's granaries opened
body: The Moot opens its granaries at Caol mhòr and Doire ghlas to the families from the west. Its minute records how much was given and the names of the families; it is one of the few Tuathaich records of the war that the library does not hold.

title: Agnes Pike's school as a shelter
body: The school at Doire ghlas that Agnes Pike founded is given over to the families from the west, and its benches serve for beds. Ellen Marsh, who teaches there, takes down the families' accounts.

title: Cnoc thais taken
body: Cnoc thais is taken after the regiments cut the road to its pits. Tom Varley's two shafts are fired and sealed. The open record gives the number of holdouts taken, and not the number who went on into the hills.

title: Onto the windy coast
body: Some of the holdouts of Cnoc thais go on beyond the hills and out onto the windy coast of the far north-west. The regiments follow them to the edge of the shire of Seann Vell and no farther. The open record names them, as it names every foe of the war, only as those 'of no shire'.

title: An dàrna cabhlach raised
body: The second fleet is raised at Seann Skell on the southern coast, to keep the eastern and southern waters while the first and fourth are in the north-west.

title: Raiders take the salt-boats
body: With the fleets drawn to the north-west, raiders from the eastern waters take two salt-boats off Àth bheag and burn a third. The second fleet runs down one of the raiders off Baile ìseal.

title: An siathamh rèisimeid raised
body: The sixth regiment is raised at Cnoc bheag, the great river port of the Hawk houses in the north-central country. It holds the northern road between the Tuathaich shires and the middle of the island, and the Hawk houses bless its colours by their own rite.

title: An dàrna rèisimeid raised
body: The second regiment is raised at Àth dhìreach in the east and set to guard the coal line and the library road. Its camp is the first soldiery the town of Muileann chaol has seen.

title: An ceathramh rèisimeid raised
body: The fourth regiment is raised at Caol bheag in the north-east. It goes down the Abhainn ghorm to Ros chiar, is shipped west round the north coast in hired dubhan hulls, and is landed at Ceann mhòr in the Tuathaich north.

title: The regiments at Ceann mhòr
body: The fourth regiment is quartered at Ceann mhòr, in the old human magistrate's house that the maor has kept since the shires were drawn. The Moot protests the quartering. The protest is received.

title: The fishermen of Cathair gheal
body: The fleets off the north-west search the fishing boats of Cathair gheal on every day they put out. The fishermen petition the Moot, and the Moot petitions the council. The searching goes on.

title: An t-ochdamh rèisimeid raised
body: The eighth regiment is raised at Inis uaine on the Abhainn chaol in the east, to guard the dubhan depots and tanks of the eastern ports, which the council fears the holdouts may fire.

title: An treas cabhlach raised
body: The third fleet is raised at Baile ghorm on the south-west coast, and carries the army's dubhan up the west coast in tank-hulls to the regiments in the hills.

title: The Baile chrom vigil
body: The Grey Night sect at Baile chrom keeps its vigil as always. The regiments quartered along the coast report a night when the whole town was dark and silent; they search it, and find nothing.

title: Àth naomh and Tobar dhearg
body: The last two western towns, Àth naomh and Tobar dhearg, open their roads to the regiments without a siege. Their pits are flooded. The open record names no holdouts taken at either.

title: An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised
body: The ninth regiment is raised at Seann Skell on the southern coast, the second town of that name in the regimental list, to guard the dubhan works the shipmasters built there. The regimental clerks tell the two apart by river and coast.

title: The column goes south
body: A column of holdouts, some hundreds strong, leaves the western hills and marches south-east through the middle of the island toward the capital. Why it did so is in the sealed archive. The Tuathaich tellings name its leader Owen Barrow. The open record gives no name.

title: The column's road
body: The column's road south-east runs by Àth bheag in the west, Muileann mhin and the edge of the capital's country. The towns it passes report it, and the open record copies their reports and not the regiments'.

title: The camp by Muileann ghlas
body: The column passes Muileann òg and camps on the fields by Muileann ghlas, a day's walk from Cathair dhearg. The first and third regiments are brought down the fair road to meet it.

title: The fair-ground emptied
body: The fair-ground at Muileann òg is cleared of its standing booths to give the first and third regiments room to camp. The books of its court for that year end with no closing entry.

title: Battle of Muileann ghlas
body: The second great battle of the war, and the last. In two summers of fighting the Tuathaich holdouts are broken: children of the humans once driven to the island's edge, driven back again, and this time by a fuel that one of their own devised.

title: The field at Muileann ghlas
body: The open record lists the first and third regiments on the field at Muileann ghlas and gives no count of the column's dead. The regiments' own dead are named on a stone at Cathair mhòr, set up the next year.

title: The last pits give up
body: Word of Muileann ghlas reaches the hills, and the holdouts still there come down to the posts of the seventh regiment on the Àth leathan road. They are disarmed and sent home. The open record counts their weapons.

title: An Cogadh Fada ends
body: The Long War ends. Nine regiments and four fleets were raised in it, each named for the town where it is stationed, and all of them stand to this day.

title: Fadachadh
body: Among Tuathaich speakers 'chaidh am fadachadh', they got long-warred, begins to be said of the defeat in the west, and then of any defeat after holding out too long. It is said as a jest, and those who say it do not laugh.

title: The regiments stay on their stations
body: The nine regiments and four fleets are not stood down. The council keeps each at the town where it was raised and pays them from the wartime tithe.

title: The market charter of Caol ruadh
body: Caol ruadh, whose harbour victualled the garrisons and the second fleet through the war, is granted a market right for the southern strait. It is the sixteenth market town, and the last chartered.

title: Dubhan's fuel over all the island
body: With the last ordered resistance gone, Dubhan's fuel is in all but law compelled upon the whole trade of the island.

title: The western seams flooded
body: By the Board's order the last western seams are flooded and their shafts capped with concrete. The seventh regiment stands by at every capping. After this no coal is dug on the island outside the Board's own works.

title: The prisoners sent home
body: The holdouts held since Muileann ghlas are let out of the capital's gaol and sent north under guard of the first regiment as far as the boundary stones. The Moot's register adds their names, in a column of their own, to the dead and maimed it has kept since the Severance.

title: Somhairle mac Lachlainn seated
body: Somhairle mac Lachlainn is given a seat on the council, the first soldier to sit there since the captains of the Severance war.

title: The seventh regiment at Àth leathan
body: The seventh regiment builds a post on the road below Àth leathan and keeps a company there. In the regimental lists it is called the Àth leathan post, and in the town something else.

title: The stone at Cathair mhòr
body: A stone is set up at Cathair mhòr bearing the names of the regiments' dead from Àth leathan and Muileann ghlas. It stands beside the market cross of the house of Mac Ùisdein.

title: The Muileann ghlas field
body: The field at Muileann ghlas where the column camped is sown again. For years the farmer who holds it finds weapons in the furrows and hands them to the first regiment, which keeps a list.

title: The library's war archive sealed
body: The whole record of the Long War at Leabharlann Muileann chaol is sealed against all readers for fifty years. No other archive in the kingdom's history has been sealed.

title: Sìleas nic Rath's open chronicle
body: Of the royal chronicle for the war years there stays open only Sìleas nic Rath's list of places, the regiments present and the counts she was allowed. Her full record went into the sealed archive with the rest.

title: The cairn at Àth leathan
body: Tuathaich families build a cairn on the field of Àth leathan without leave. The patrols of the seventh regiment leave it standing, and every time they pass it has grown by a stone or two.

title: The tithe carried forward
body: The Treasury's accounts carry the wartime tithe forward as a standing line under the regiments' pay. No minute of the council records a choice to keep it.

title: The market-due fixed
body: The Treasury fixes the market-due at seventeen in the hundred on every sale a town makes into its market and on every sale between markets. A clerk of the Treasury is set in each of the sixteen market towns to take it and keep the market roll. The wartime tithe on dubhan stays at the pumps, on its own line.

title: The Fuel-Fitters and the regiments
body: The Guild of Fuel-Fitters at Seann Skell on the southern coast is given the contract for the regiments' engines and the fleets' hulls, and doubles its rolls. The charter rule holds, and all its new fitters are Dia-thìrich.

title: The regiments' arms contracts
body: The forges of Àth naomh in the west and Caol ìseal on the north coast, which smelt the bog-iron of their districts, take the Crown's contract for the regiments' small arms and field-guns. The forge-towns of the old vein country follow. Arms become the dearest common goods in every market of the kingdom.

title: The second fleet off Baile ìseal
body: The second fleet runs down off Baile ìseal the raiders who took the salt-boats in the war, and brings their hulls into Seann Skell. The lighthouse log at Baile ìseal records the chase from the lamp-room.

title: The fourth fleet in the north-west
body: The fourth fleet, kept on the Tuathaich coast after the war, searches the raiders' bays off Cathair gheal and finds them empty. The fishermen of Cathair gheal say the raiders left when the fleets came and will return when they go.

title: The third fleet's tank-hulls
body: The third fleet at Baile ghorm keeps its tank-hulls after the war and runs dubhan up the west coast to the Tuathaich depots on the council's contract. The Moot pays the freight.

title: The creature off the cape again
body: The fourth fleet's log for the year records a thing longer than a patrol boat off the north-west cape, where the Tuathaich fishermen reported one in Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's day. The log calls it a whale.

title: Anna nic Phàil's motion
body: The motion to make amends to the Tuathaich is brought into the council by Anna nic Phàil, councillor for Cathair dhomhain, on a petition of the Moot under Martha Greaves. She speaks for it once.

title: The motion for amends
body: In the capital it is proposed to pay the Tuathaich for their losses in the war. The motion is let die quietly, and no vote is taken.

title: The Moot's minute on the amends
body: The Moot's minute on the motion for amends runs to one line: 'Allowed to die.' That same year Martha Greaves lays down the chair. The Moot chooses Peter Hale, a great-grandson of its first speaker, to follow her.

title: The fifth regiment's barracks
body: The fifth regiment builds stone barracks at Seann Warr, the first lasting quarters any of the nine regiments has had. The town gives the land and takes the regiment's custom.

title: The eighth regiment at Inis uaine
body: The eighth regiment's guard on the eastern dubhan tanks at Inis uaine is made lasting. Its officers take houses in the town, and the Seann Spioradan house of Inis uaine adds the regiment to its prayers.

title: The fourth regiment leaves Ceann mhòr
body: The fourth regiment leaves the old magistrate's house at Ceann mhòr and goes home to Caol bheag. The Moot asks that the house be given to the town. It is given to the maor.

title: Seann-chunntas
body: Tuathaich speakers begin to name the tabled request to the library and the dead motion for amends together as 'seann-chunntas', an old reckoning that none in power will settle and none has cancelled. The Dia-thìrich in office do not take up the word.

title: The Sloc Mòr closed
body: The Mine Board shuts the upper galleries of the Sloc Mòr at Achadh dhomhain. One face is kept open in the Rite's keeping, to cut coal for the altars, a few baskets a year.

title: The last hewers
body: Twelve hewers are kept at the Sloc Mòr to cut the altar-coal in the Rite's keeping. They are the last of their trade to work the vein on the island, and the Rite gives them its own oath, not the dissolved guild's.

title: The regiments at the Còmhrag
body: Fighters of the regiments are entered in the Còmhrag at Ceann leathan for the first time. The ninth regiment's man wins it. The fair-wardens raise the gate-price again.

title: The second regiment's library guard
body: The second regiment at Àth dhìreach keeps a guard at Leabharlann Muileann chaol over the sealed war archive. The keeper, Raghnall mac Mhuirich, writes to the council that the library did not ask for one.

title: The coal line carries no coal
body: The last coal train runs from Achadh dhomhain to Cathair dhearg. The coal line keeps its name and carries dubhan, wool and soldiers.

title: The sixth regiment on the northern road
body: The sixth regiment at Cnoc bheag keeps posts on the northern road where the boundary stones stand. For the first time since the Severance the Tuathaich going south must show a pass. The council's minute calls the passes for a time only.

title: The fair of the present year
body: The fair at Muileann òg draws traders from every shire the state holds. Tuathaich wool is sold there on its northern day, through Dia-thìrich factors, as it has been since the first fair.

title: The Còmhrag of the present year
body: The Còmhrag at Ceann leathan is fought with staves and fists, as it has been since edged tools were banned. Two regiments and nine shires send fighters. One man dies.

title: The eleven books
body: Ellen Marsh's eleven books are copied by hand in the Tuathaich schools and kept in the north. The library's catalogue lists the tabled request, and not the books.

title: The Moot of the present year
body: The Moot at Caol mhòr meets under Peter Hale. Its minute-books run unbroken from Walter Hale's first meeting. It has no standing in Dia-thìrich law and has never asked for any.

title: The dubhan works of the present
body: Dubhan is made at Seann Skell on the southern coast and at works in the east and north. Every lamp, engine, ship and lorry on the island runs on it. The coin is pegged to it, and the tithe is taken on every sale.

title: The Treasury's roll of the present year
body: The Treasury's roll for the year stands at 9,568 purses: 6,375 from the head-due, taken at eighteen purses on every hundred thousand heads, and 3,193 from the market-due, taken at seventeen in the hundred on every sale. The wartime tithe is carried on its own line under the regiments' pay. The windy coast pays neither due.

title: Dubhan's charter of export
body: Dubhan, who made the first working fuel and is now in his sixty-ninth year, wins from the council at Cathair dhearg, after a year of letters and three sittings, leave to sell dubhan beyond the island. It is the first leave the kingdom has given since the Severance for any good of Dia-thìr to pass beyond its waters. The charter is narrow. The Treasury sets each year's measure. The fuel is loaded only at Ros dhomhain, where a clerk of the Treasury takes the tithe on every barrel. The kingdom's depots and the Moot's are served first. Nothing of the vein goes with it: the vein's coal is not sold, and the custodians of Òrd Bhrìde seal every hold. Dubhan has told neither the council nor the chronicler who buys from him. In the autumn the first tank-hull loaded under the charter goes out past the western capes, and on the day she sails the priests of Manannan at Seann Skell say their prayer to keep the sea shut.

title: The altar-coal
body: The Rite's twelve hewers at the Sloc Mòr cut the year's altar-coal. It fills four baskets. The high custodian at Seann Skell shares it among the houses of the Rite by lot.

title: The chronicler's note on the present
body: Sìleas nic Rath writes at the foot of the year that the kingdom's record is whole in every part but two: the war, which is sealed, and the north, which was not asked.

title: The present
body: The coal is all but gone. The trade of the island runs on a name that once belonged to one man. The Dia-thìrich hold the capital and the sea. The Tuathaich hold the north, a grievance five years old, their Church, and the memory of the First Canoe, Naomh Breandan's voyage to the Isle of the Blessed, which the people who have twice defeated them still call folklore.
